intervention: Integrated soil-crop system management delivered through a national researcher-extension network
mechanism: 13,000+ field trials → locally specific recommendations → 1,152 researchers working with extension and agribusiness
why: Dense trial network and decision-support translated into simple local recommendations; strong public extension.
conditions: Large state research system; stable institutions; fertilizer overuse baseline.
transfer_reason: The principle (local trials → price-aware recommendations → mass delivery) transfers; Myanmar lacks the trial network and public extension, so delivery would rely on phone panels and private digital platforms.
required_modification: Use existing plot-level panel data plus targeted trials; deliver through digital advisory apps.
title: China: Integrated soil-crop system management delivered through a national researcher-extension network

mechanism: Certified seed (must do) plus reductions in seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water and post-harvest loss
adoption: Most surveyed farmers adopted at least one practice; used >8 years on average (465 farmers, An Giang & Can Tho)
impact: Farmers perceived lower input use and livelihood gains
Seed and fertilizer rates remained particularly high - overuse persists
why: Simple, memorable package backed by provincial extension.
conditions: Strong public extension and irrigated, intensive systems.
transfer_reason: Myanmar's problem is often under- or mistimed use rather than overuse, and extension is weaker; the packaging lesson transfers, not the reductions.
required_modification: Reframe as 'right rate, right time' under price shocks.
title: Vietnam: '1 Must Do, 5 Reductions' (1M5R) national programme

intervention: Mechanized direct seeding (mDSR) adopted into national low-emission rice strategy
mechanism: Row/precision seeders via companies and cooperatives; national technical guidelines (Oct 2023)
adoption: 350 ha planned in 3 provinces (summer-autumn 2024); national 1 million ha low-emission rice target by 2030
why: Private service companies plus government endorsement.
transfer_reason: Myanmar already direct-seeds ~50-75% of farms by broadcasting (S301); precision seeding could recover the perceived yield penalty while keeping labour savings, but needs service providers and fuel.
required_modification: Service-provider model through existing combine/tractor outsourcing networks.
title: Vietnam: Mechanized direct seeding (mDSR) adopted into national low-emission rice strategy

mechanism: Market-driven machinery services; Mekong Delta held ~75% of Vietnam's harvesters by 2014
adoption: National share of rice harvested by combines 15% (2006) → 35% (2013)
impact: Harvesting 'almost fully mechanised' in Vietnam and Cambodia by 2019 (IRRI)
why: Labour scarcity plus private service provision.
transfer_reason: Myanmar followed the same path 2011-2020 (S162); the lesson is sustaining services under fuel and security shocks.
required_modification: None for the model; risk management for fuel/insecurity.
title: Vietnam: Combine-harvester diffusion via private services

mechanism: AWD pipes and training; prepaid volumetric irrigation cards
cost: Pipe marginal cost ~133 taka; demand fell to zero below that
adoption: Low installation (1.4% control vs 7.4% treated above 60 taka)
impact: No water saving under seasonal per-acre water charges
Under volumetric pricing: standing water -18%, profit +~7% (1,870 taka/acre)
why: Works only where farmers pay for water by volume.
transfer_reason: Benefits depend on volumetric water pricing; Myanmar canal schemes rarely price water volumetrically - pump schemes (diesel) are the plausible niche.
required_modification: Target diesel-pump irrigated summer rice where pumping cost is borne per hour.
title: Bangladesh: Alternate wetting and drying (cluster RCTs)

cost: BDT 1,595 crore (~US$163 m); >35,000 machines, ~9,000 combines (84% of value)
impact: High-allocation areas: yields +6-13%, labour costs -38-70%, production costs -12-26% (earlier causal analysis as cited)
transfer_reason: Myanmar mechanized without subsidies through private outsourcing (S162); a large subsidy is fiscally and institutionally unrealistic now.
title: Bangladesh: Combine-harvester purchase subsidy programme (Phase III)

mechanism: 5 kg seed minikits to farmers in 64 randomly selected villages
impact: ~45% higher yield after 10 days of submergence
No significant yield penalty without flooding
Larger benefits for low-lying, disadvantaged farmers
why: Variety directly addresses submergence without trade-off.
transfer_reason: Delta flood losses are large (S302); transfer depends on locally adapted tolerant varieties and seed system capacity (P09). Myanmar availability of Sub1 varieties was not verified in this build.
required_modification: Verify locally released flood-tolerant varieties; couple with seed system.
title: India: Submergence-tolerant Swarna-Sub1 variety (RCT, Odisha)

intervention: Rice Crop Manager site-specific nutrient advice (Odisha on-farm trials)
mechanism: Digital decision tool generating field-specific N-P-K-Zn advice
impact: P rates -8.6 to -18.1 kg/ha; N higher in kharif, lower in rabi
why: Corrects nutrient imbalance (adds K and Zn).
transfer_reason: Myanmar has an RCM prototype (S112) that never scaled; delivery via private digital advisory (I04) could substitute for state extension.
required_modification: Recalibrate with Myanmar response data; add price-ratio logic.
title: India: Rice Crop Manager site-specific nutrient advice (Odisha on-farm trials)

mechanism: Soil testing and card-based fertilizer recommendation
impact: Government-commissioned study reports chemical fertilizer -8-10% and paddy cost of cultivation -16-25%
transfer_reason: Requires lab network absent in Myanmar; evidence is a non-experimental government study (low confidence).
required_modification: Replace lab testing with response-based recommendations.
title: India: Soil Health Card scheme

intervention: Thai Rice NAMA / Thai Rice project (laser levelling, AWD, SSNM, straw management)
mechanism: Training, service providers, 50% subsidy for farmers
cost: EUR 14.9 m provided; EUR 14 m leveraged
adoption: 79,275 households; 319,526 ha; 2,544 farmer groups; 99,094 farmers trained
why: Bundled finance, service providers and training.
transfer_reason: Relies on donor carbon finance and stable institutions; laser levelling services are scarce in Myanmar.
title: Thailand: Thai Rice NAMA / Thai Rice project (laser levelling, AWD, SSNM, straw management)

mechanism: Area-based disaster-declared indemnity; payment to bank accounts
conditions: Universal banking of farmers via BAAC.
transfer_reason: Myanmar's formal credit and banking contracted after 2021 (S286); index insurance remains at proposal stage (I06).
required_modification: Basis-risk testing with satellite and MAPS yield data first.
title: Thailand: National rice cultivation insurance (BAAC/TGIA)

intervention: ADB-IRRI postharvest project (flatbed dryers, hermetic storage, combines)
impact: Loss and quality impacts not quantified in source
transfer_reason: Modern Myanmar mills already vertically integrate services (S305); dryers fit miller-led models.
title: Cambodia: ADB-IRRI postharvest project (flatbed dryers, hermetic storage, combines)

intervention: On-farm variety and fertilizer trials with World Vision (Savannakhet)
mechanism: Volunteer trial farms, seed swaps, district extension
adoption: ~22,654 potential beneficiaries (~47% of farms in six districts)
impact: Fertilizer use stayed very low due to cost
why: Trusted embedded trials plus seed multiplication.
transfer_reason: NGO-embedded trials work in low-state-capacity settings similar to post-2021 Myanmar; fertilizer affordability remained binding.
title: Laos: On-farm variety and fertilizer trials with World Vision (Savannakhet)

intervention: Irrigation access for sticky rice (LECS panel, PSM and DID)
adoption: ~20% of farm households had irrigation access
transfer_reason: Supports investing in reliable water delivery; Myanmar's issue is scheme performance (P10), not just access.
title: Laos: Irrigation access for sticky rice (LECS panel, PSM and DID)
